title: Linear Functions, Part 3: Traps and the Fast Way

beats.say: In this video, we look at five mistakes that students make with linear functions, then a fast way to find a line from two points using Desmos.
Each trap is shown as a wrong line first, then the right line, with the reason that students fall for it.

scenes.title: Trap 1: do not flip the slope

beats.say: Trap one. Slope is rise over run, the change in y over the change in x. A common mistake is to put the change in x on top.
beats.wrong_why: Run over rise is upside down

beats.say: The change in y goes on top. For the points two comma five and six comma seventeen, that is seventeen minus five over six minus two, which is three.
Trap two. If you start the top subtraction with the second point, you must start the bottom subtraction with the second point as well. Mixing the order flips the sign of the answer.
Use the same order on top and on bottom. Seventeen minus five is twelve, and six minus two is four, so the slope is positive three, not negative three.
Trap three. Suppose f of x equals two x plus one, and the question asks for what x does f of x equal four. Students plug four in as the input.
beats.wrong_why: That puts 4 in as the input

beats.say: Here four is the output, so we set two x plus one equal to four and solve. Two x equals three, so x equals one point five.
Trap four. Consider D of t equals nine hundred minus twenty-five t, the number of liters left in a tank after t minutes. Answer choices often call the twenty-five an increase.
The slope is negative twenty-five. The amount decreases by twenty-five liters every minute, and nine hundred is the starting amount.

scenes.title: Trap 5: intercept is not the rate

beats.say: Trap five. In C of n equals thirty-two plus five n, students sometimes say the cost per session is thirty-two dollars, because it is the first number they see.
The number that multiplies n is the rate. Each session costs five dollars. The thirty-two is a one-time base fee.
For two clean points, the slope formula plus one substitution is faster than typing. Desmos helps when numbers are messy, or when the question gives a table.
Our example is the gym again. Three sessions cost forty-seven dollars, and eight sessions cost seventy-two dollars. We want the equation of the line.
We will enter the two points in a table and ask Desmos for the line that fits them.
Create a table with x values three and eight, and y values forty-seven and seventy-two. Each row appears as a point.
Type y sub one, a tilde, then m times x sub one plus b. Use the right arrow after each subscript to leave it.
Desmos reports m equals five and b equals thirty-two. So the line is y equals five x plus thirty-two, matching what we found by hand.
Now a practice problem. The function f of x equals four x minus nine. Find f of negative two, and find the value of x for which f of x equals fifteen. Pause and try it first.

card.sub: Find f(−2), and x when f(x) = 15

beats.say: Substitute negative two for x. Notice that this asks for an output, because the input is given.
Four times negative two is negative eight. So the expression becomes negative eight minus nine.
Negative eight minus nine is negative seventeen. So f of negative two equals negative seventeen.
Now the output is given as fifteen, so we set the expression equal to fifteen and solve for the input.
Add nine to both sides, so the plain number leaves the left side. Fifteen plus nine is twenty-four.
Divide both sides by four. Twenty-four divided by four is six. So x equals six.
Check both. Four times negative two minus nine is negative seventeen. And four times six minus nine is fifteen. Both answers are correct.
To recap. Slope is rise over run, with the same order on top and bottom, and the number that multiplies the input is the rate.
Evaluate when the input is given, and solve when the output is given. A negative rate means the amount decreases.
Use Desmos regression when numbers are messy. In the next topic, we study linear equations in two variables.
